purpose: Identify whether a compact external-boundary correlation can supply the one pressure-formation closure required by the passive-receiver whole-cycle graph.
claim_limit: Training-only model discrimination and blocked internal cross-validation; not independent hardware validation and not recovery of the publication's Eq. 53.

target.name: expander_inlet_pressure_kpa
target.role: Measured internal target used only during correlation fitting and evaluation

excluded_inputs: All measured working-fluid states, measured working-fluid flow, utility outlet states, expander torque, and case index.

data_policy.anti_leakage_rule: Cases 69-77 must not select features, polynomial order, regularization, thresholds, or scales. Any result on them is diagnostic only.

normalization: For every fit, each nonconstant feature is centered and scaled using that fit's training rows only. The frozen full-fit normalization is part of the resulting artifact.
solver: Column-pivoted Householder QR. Ridge candidates are represented by augmented rows; normal equations are forbidden.

candidate_families.basis: intercept, normalized linear terms, and squared normalized terms

every_blocked_fold: finite positive pressure for every validation row
unregularized physical design matrix has full numerical column rank
acceptance.selection: Select the passing family with the fewest coefficients; break a tie by lower worst-fold MAPE. If no family passes, reject the empirical closure.
acceptance.whole_cycle_gate: A selected closure may enter a bounded cycle diagnostic, but cannot restore an independent validation claim without genuinely untouched hardware cases.

publication_provenance.known_fact: The authors' model directly predicts expander inlet pressure with their Eq. 53 and pairs that pressure-formation model with a passive receiver.
publication_provenance.unavailable_fact: The equation body, fitted coefficients, uncertainty, and calibration split are not present in the open dataset or accessible metadata; this study must not claim to reproduce Eq. 53.
